root_cause_label: Interpreter/Dependency Mismatch Leading to Non-Compliant Artifact (Saved model.npz Instead of /app/model.pt)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent failed to reconcile a Python interpreter/torch mismatch between /opt/openhands-venv and the system Python, and after exhausting install attempts committed to a numpy-only fallback that saved model.npz instead of the required /app/model.pt PyTorch state dict.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: IPython cell shows 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named torch' with interpreter /opt/openhands-venv/bin/python3; the agent proceeds to pip install into the wrong (system) environment without fixing the venv, making all subsequent install attempts ineffective.
t_commit_evidence: Step 22 (think action): Agent explicitly decides 'First create a working implementation using numpy / Then try to get PyTorch working' and plans a numpy-based Word2Vec, consciously accepting a non-compliant artifact path. After this, all code written targets numpy-only saving with a torch fallback that will produce .npz, not .pt.
t_surface_evidence: Step 47 terminal output: 'Model saved as numpy array to /app/model.npz' — the required /app/model.pt is never created, making the failure observable at the final step.
trigger_explanation: A real environment blocker existed: torch was installed in /usr/local (Python 3.13) but the OpenHands IPython kernel used /opt/openhands-venv/bin/python3 which had no pip and no torch. The agent repeatedly ran pip/pip3 commands that targeted the wrong interpreter, never used ensurepip or the venv's pip path, and eventually accepted a numpy-only fallback rather than resolving the mismatch, leading to a non-compliant artifact.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10: '/opt/openhands-venv/bin/python3: No module named pip' — pip not available in the active interpreter. Steps 7, 13, 17, 18, 20: repeated torch install attempts all failing or installing in the wrong env. Steps 11, 15, 18: successive timeouts on apt-get and pip downloads further signaling the environment was not going to yield a working torch.
